general-linux.reason: Shared and normally CPU-busy. Valid for work whose result does not depend on wall-clock speed; no result measured here may enter a performance claim, a regression trend, or an engine ranking.

bench-solo.reason: One owned machine, quiet by construction: cores held off the scheduler, SMT disabled, one job at a time, and attested against the kernel before a run builds anything.

qualification.attested_by: tools/run-dedicated-benchmark.js compares the machine's own report against the frozen config before shipping, including that every pinned core is in /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated

repeatability.method: Revision pairs that compile to byte-identical binaries, so the figure assumes no model of what counts as equivalent work.
repeatability.caveat: Quote it per workload, not as one number: spread scales inversely with per-unit cost, from 0.32% worst on dense_tables at 39us/unit to 5.74% on closures_upvalues at 372ns/unit. This belongs to the backfill protocol's five repetitions; the A/B acceptance protocol runs 101-201 and is far tighter.

measurement.reason: No timer may start a billed instance. The retired cloud matrix remains reachable by explicit dispatch only, because it is still the sole producer of the cross-engine reference every published Rustia number is normalised against.

publication.reason: Accepted committed benchmark artifacts are validated and published automatically without taking measurements or creating cloud resources.
publication.next_action: Keep the artifact-only publisher healthy and investigate any failed publication before accepting newer public results.

progress.next_action: Measure the newest pending performance-relevant commit on the owned benchmark host.

landscape.reason: Immutable latest-stable landscape campaigns and engine-version bridges are not implemented yet.
landscape.next_action: Add version provenance, immutable landscape snapshots, and old/new reference bridge validation before enabling monthly refreshes.
